contentPolicy: Original micro-prompts and methods, not copied past-paper wording.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Eliminate wrong units and powers of ten before exact arithmetic.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not pick the closest-looking number before checking units.
cards.front: For a four-option calculation, what should you do before looking at the choices?
cards.back: Estimate the answer and units independently.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Use N=kg m s⁻² and J=kg m² s⁻².
cards.paper2Pitfall: A number can be correct with the wrong physical dimensions.
cards.front: What is a quick way to test the SI units of an unfamiliar expression?
cards.back: Replace each quantity by its base units.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Use a symbolic ratio before substituting numbers.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not square the wrong factor.
cards.front: In a ratio question, how can you avoid large calculations?
cards.back: Divide the two formulas and cancel common constants.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Compare to a nearby power-of-ten midpoint where needed.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A factor of 10 error changes the chosen option.
cards.front: For an order-of-magnitude choice, what should be checked?
cards.back: The nearest power of ten after comparing sizes.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Square-root the tension multiplier: √9=3.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not multiply frequency by 9.
cards.front: When tension is multiplied by 9, how does first-harmonic frequency change?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Keep μ and T constant while comparing.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not double the frequency.
cards.front: If string vibrating length doubles and tension stays fixed, what happens to frequency?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: N×s is change in momentum.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Force–displacement gives work, not impulse.
cards.front: Which graph area gives impulse?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Subtract areas below the time axis.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Distance is total absolute area, not signed displacement.
cards.front: Which graph area gives the displacement?
cards.back: Signed area under a velocity–time graph.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Use signed velocity changes.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A position-time gradient is velocity.
cards.front: Which graph gradient gives acceleration?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Velocity zero does not imply acceleration zero.
cards.paper2Method: Acceleration remains −g for upwards-positive convention.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not set both v and a to zero.
cards.front: At the top of a vertical throw, what acceleration acts without air resistance?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: v∝√h.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not multiply speed by four.
cards.front: How does free-fall speed change if fall distance becomes four times as large?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Choose a positive direction before adding momenta.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not add speed magnitudes as if directions matched.
cards.front: For a constant-momentum collision, when are signs essential?
cards.back: Whenever bodies move in opposite directions.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Ideal ammeter causes no voltage drop.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Infinite resistance is for an ideal voltmeter.
cards.front: What does an ideal ammeter have?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Ideal voltmeter draws no current.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Zero resistance would short the component.
cards.front: What does an ideal voltmeter have?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: At constant V, power ∝1/R.
cards.paper2Pitfall: At fixed I the result would instead double.
cards.front: If a resistor is at fixed pd and its resistance doubles, how does its power change?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Do not use P=V²/R as if V stayed fixed.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Always note what is held constant.
cards.front: At fixed current, if resistance triples, what happens to power?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Use direction signs before solving.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not count all arrows as leaving.
cards.front: How is junction current found when some arrows enter and others leave?
cards.back: Total entering current equals total leaving current.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Resistances are in series for a simple loop.
cards.paper2Method: Use total emf over total resistance.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use ε/R unless r is negligible.
cards.front: A cell with emf ε and internal resistance r has external resistor R. What is I?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: 1/Rtotal=1/R+1/R.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Total resistance is not twice R.
cards.front: When two equal resistors are in parallel, how does their combined resistance compare?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Diameter ×2 gives area ×4.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not halve resistance only.
cards.front: When wire diameter doubles (same length and metal), how does resistance change?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Mean free path decreases as scattering increases.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not apply thermistor behaviour to a metal.
cards.front: For a metallic conductor heated up, what happens to resistivity?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Read circuit arrangement before predicting current.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Metallic resistor behaviour is the opposite.
cards.front: An NTC thermistor gets hotter. What happens to resistance?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Then trace effect through potential divider.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not assume Vout always decreases regardless of location.
cards.front: An LDR receives more light. What happens to its resistance?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Current can flow with negligible resistance.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not say merely 'very small' for ideal superconductivity.
cards.front: What does a superconducting material's resistivity do below its critical temperature?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Frequency stays fixed; wavelength decreases.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not say frequency decreases at boundary.
cards.front: For refraction into a higher refractive index, what happens to light speed?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: λglass≈λair/1.5.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Wavelength is not unchanged.
cards.front: What happens to the wavelength of light in glass with n=1.5 versus air?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Same frequency alone is not enough.
cards.paper2Method: State a constant relative phase.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Independent lamps are not automatically coherent.
cards.front: What is a necessary condition for stable interference fringes?
cards.back: Coherent sources with constant phase difference.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Check any source phase offset before using rule.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use half-integer λ for maxima.
cards.front: What path difference gives constructive interference for in-phase sources?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Minimum intensity for equal amplitudes.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Integer λ gives constructive interference.
cards.front: What path difference gives destructive interference for in-phase sources?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: One-quarter cycle is 90°.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not confuse distance with angle.
cards.front: A path difference is λ/4. What is phase difference?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Antinode to adjacent node is λ/4.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use λ for adjacent nodes.
cards.front: What is separation of adjacent nodes in a stationary wave?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: There is a node between them.
cards.paper2Method: Phase difference π.
cards.paper2Pitfall: They are not in phase.
cards.front: How do two adjacent antinodes on a stationary string move?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Sound in air is longitudinal and cannot be polarised.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Interference and diffraction can affect both types.
cards.front: Which waves can be polarised: transverse or longitudinal?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Compare λ divided by slit width.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A wider slit narrows the maximum.
cards.front: For diffraction through a narrow slit, what change widens the central maximum?
cards.back: Decreasing slit width or increasing wavelength.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Speed and wavelength change.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not scale frequency with n.
cards.front: If light moves to a medium with n higher, does its frequency change?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: One photon can release one electron.
cards.paper2Method: Kmax=hf−φ; photon rate controls electron rate if all else unchanged.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not claim current rises simply because photons have more energy.
cards.front: For photoelectric effect at fixed photon rate, what happens when frequency rises above threshold?
cards.back: Maximum kinetic energy rises; emission rate may stay similar.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: One low-energy photon cannot overcome work function.
cards.paper2Pitfall: More low-energy photons do not rescue the effect.
cards.front: If incident light has frequency below threshold, can higher intensity eject electrons?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Use h in J s, f in Hz.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use kinetic energy of a mass.
cards.front: Which equation gives energy of a photon from frequency?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: At nonrelativistic speeds p=mv.
cards.paper2Pitfall: The wavelength is not set by particle charge.
cards.front: What determines de Broglie wavelength for a slow moving particle?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Mass and speeds may differ.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Equal wavelength does not mean equal speed.
cards.front: Two particles have same de Broglie wavelength. Which property must match?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A neutron turns into a proton.
cards.paper2Method: Nucleon number stays unchanged.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not decrease atomic number.
cards.front: In beta-minus decay, what happens to proton number?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A proton changes to a neutron.
cards.paper2Method: Mass number stays the same.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not change nucleon number.
cards.front: In beta-plus decay, what happens to proton number?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Mesons have a quark–antiquark pair.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not count antiquark pairs as three.
cards.front: How many quarks are in an ordinary baryon?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Proton uud has charge +e.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not interchange the signs.
cards.front: What are the quark charges of u and d?
cards.back: u is +2/3 e; d is −1/3 e.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: d→u+W⁻, then W⁻→e⁻+antineutrino.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not swap W⁻ with W⁺.
cards.front: What is the charge of the exchange particle in beta-minus decay?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Photoelectric emission demonstrates photon particle energy.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not say photoelectric effect itself proves continuous waves.
cards.front: Which particle evidence is wave-like: diffraction or photoelectric emission?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Use positive magnitude of energy level difference.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use a negative emitted frequency.
cards.front: For an atom emitting light on a downward energy transition, how is frequency found?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Use combinations if all transitions allowed.
cards.paper2Method: For four levels, there are up to six distinct transitions.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Coincident energy gaps can reduce unique frequencies.
cards.front: How do you count distinct emitted photon energies from four allowed levels?
cards.back: Count distinct possible downward level pairs.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Use linear elastic section.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Not stiffness of a wire (which is F/e).
cards.front: Which quantity is represented by the gradient of a stress–strain graph in linear region?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: With elastic loading it is stored strain energy.
cards.paper2Pitfall: The gradient gives spring constant in linear region.
cards.front: What does area under a force–displacement curve give?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Acceleration is zero at steady speed.
cards.paper2Method: Resistive and driving forces balance.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Terminal speed does not mean all individual forces vanish.
cards.front: For an object at terminal velocity, what is the resultant force?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A couple is equal opposite parallel forces.
cards.paper2Method: Moment has units N m.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not use half the arm unless it is explicitly half the separation.
cards.front: For a force couple, what gives its moment?
cards.back: One force × perpendicular separation of the two force lines.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Geometry affects stiffness, not E.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not equate force/extension for different dimensions.
cards.front: Two rods have the same E. Which ratio is equal for both under elastic loading?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Add resistive power F_resistive v if present.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Power is not mgh without dividing by time.
cards.front: A car travels uphill at constant speed. What power helps oppose a slope?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Method: Label node voltages and current directions.
cards.paper2Pitfall: A crossing wire is not always a junction.
cards.front: How can you spot a multiple-choice trap involving a circuit diagram?
cards.back: Check parallel and series topology before any calculation.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A sanity check catches arithmetic traps.
cards.paper2Method: Ask whether the answer increases or decreases as expected.
cards.paper2Pitfall: Do not change a justified answer just because another looks familiar.
cards.front: In a one-mark MCQ with four options, what final check is fastest?
cards.back: Check units, sign and limiting case.
